title: Conversion to a three-literal satisfiability test
statement: Let $T$ be a family of three-variable linear-equation testers, one for each positive number of variables, and suppose the corresponding sign testers form a dictator-versus-no-notables test with parameters $0<\alpha<\beta\leq 1$ and error function $\lambda$. If $3/4+\alpha/4<\beta$, then replacing each tester by its associated three-literal satisfiability tester gives a dictator-versus-no-notables test with allowed predicates consisting of all three-literal disjunctions, lower parameter $3/4+\alpha/4$, upper parameter $\beta$, and error function $\lambda(\varepsilon)/4$.
hypotheses_covered: A family T of three-variable linear-equation testers for each positive number of variables
The associated sign testers satisfy all conditions of a dictator-versus-no-notables test for the linear-equation predicate family, with parameters α, β, and error function λ
